lights.sourceNote: The Allied TBM flare-layer's delayed parachute flare (ASW/convoy-escort manual, illumination-flare attack; M24 per TM 9-981). It ignites 3 s before the mission clock starts (the opening scene shows the ignition; a flight with no opening finds it already burning) and the 150 s burn (the M24 candle burns 3 min) is authored: it IS the attack window (release.window, scheduled lights follow the mission clock: NightFacts.clockOriginTick); a test holds the two equal.

J4 opening-scene lighting (F10D, 2026-10-17): authored scenery for the surface engagement the Navy Chronology records; no layout is claimed. A gun flash is a half-second fixture on a negative mission time, so it shows in the opening and never in the flight.

objectives.label: Torpedo a destroyer under the flare
Clear the bay to the west

then.message: Strike lead: the flare is lit over the bay. Torpedo a Fletcher inside its light, keep clear of the transport, then clear the bay to the west.
The flare is dying. Clear the bay to the west.

briefing.situation: Ormoc Bay, 3 December 1944, 2130, no moon worth the name. American destroyers are shelling the port and a Japanese transport is still afloat off the pier. A flare-laying TBM has lit the bay for one short window. You are a Navy B5N2 with one torpedo, west of the bay: come in from the west, drop on a Fletcher while the flare burns, keep the transport alive and clear the bay to the west. There is no field to land at: crossing the western gate is the recovery.

history.text: On the night of 3 December 1944 American and Japanese destroyers fought in Ormoc Bay and USS Cooper was lost to torpedoes. This mission is inspired by that action, not a reconstruction of it: the lone Kate, its attack window and the American flare-laying TBM are invented for the game, and the ship layout is a gameplay compression. A ditching near friendly ships ends the sortie in a normal debrief but earns no badge.
